clue.text: Withdrawing from European area held by cartel

indicators.note: something held by another sits inside it, so the cartel word wraps round the rest

parts.note: a ring is a group of dealers acting together to fix prices
standard abbreviation for European
a tract is an expanse of land

explanation.surface: Someone pulls out of a European region controlled by a price-fixing cartel.
explanation.walkthrough: A ring is a group of traders who secretly agree prices, which makes 'cartel' fair; 'held by' looks like ownership but is the enclosing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to pull back or take back, so retracting is a synonym for withdrawing.

clue.text: What's behind strange power cut?

parts.note: rum is an old-fashioned British word for odd or peculiar
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about the cause of an odd power outage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power cut' reads as a blackout, but 'cut' is a second definition: rump is a cut of beef, as well as the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: The rump is an animal's or person's hindquarters, and rump steak is a butcher's cut from that part.

clue.text: Pet gent spoilt — guy's attached to it

indicators.note: something spoilt is ruined or messed up, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A pampered gentleman, and some fellow tied to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man, but here it is a guy rope, the line that steadies a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy rope is tied off to a stake driven into the ground, which is exactly what this camping item is.

clue.text: Misplaced caution over captain's position in game

indicators.note: things misplaced are put in the wrong spot, so these letters are moved around
in a down clue, one part over another simply comes first, on top

parts.note: letters of caution rearranged
a ship's captain commands from the bridge

explanation.surface: A skipper's lost caution about where he stands during some game.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an older form of the card game in which partners bid for the contract, the forerunner of contract play.

clue.text: Score with little time left before close of play

indicators.note: one part comes before the next, so they are simply placed in sequence

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
left in the sense of departed

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the last letter of play

explanation.surface: A cricket or football total with the clock running down before the end of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like remaining time, but it means went, as in departed.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is an old word for a set of twenty, as in 'three score years and ten'.

clue.text: Like most pages in books, feeling less edited

parts.note: more numb, that is having less feeling
ED is the abbreviation for edited

explanation.surface: A book's pages, and someone who feels flat after their work has been edited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' here is the comparative of numb, read as num-ber, not the noun for a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Book pages normally carry page figures, so most of them are marked in sequence.

clue.text: Section of staff is helping one or more in school

indicators.note: a section is a piece cut from a longer run, so the letters lie within these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of staff, all of is, and the start of helping

explanation.surface: Some school staff helping one or more pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like an educational institution but is a group of fish swimming together.
explanation.definitionFit: A school is a shoal of fish, and the plural of the word is unchanged, so one or more members fits.

clue.text: Check bug around start of program

indicators.note: one word goes around another, enclosing it

parts.note: a bug is an insect

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: first letter of program

explanation.surface: Check a software bug at the very beginning of a program.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' and 'program' suggest computing, but the bug is a creeping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect something is to examine it closely, the same as checking it.

clue.text: Acrobatic performance — watch parts

parts.note: the fragment names a timepiece whose parts are wanted: a hand and a spring
says the timepiece is to be taken as two of its components

explanation.surface: Come and watch the bits of an acrobatic show.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts are a hand, which points to the time, and a mainspring, which drives a mechanical watch; joined they name the gymnastic move.
explanation.definitionFit: A handspring is a gymnastic leap in which the body flips over on the hands, a classic tumbling move.

clue.text: Clap in irons a salt interrupting the person speaking

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one part sits inside another

parts.note: the speaker refers to themself as me
taken as written
NaCl is the chemical formula for common salt, sodium chloride

explanation.surface: A sailor is clapped in irons for interrupting someone giving a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like an old sailor, the usual crossword sense, but here it is the chemical formula for table salt.
explanation.definitionFit: A manacle is a handcuff or shackle, and as a verb it means to put such irons on someone.

clue.text: Crazy is running for president

parts.note: mad means crazy
taken as written
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A cynical remark on someone who campaigns for the presidency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running for president' reads as standing for election, but running is just ON.
explanation.definitionFit: James Madison was the fourth President of the United States, so the surname is an example of a president.

clue.text: Withdrawing bad design, with representative protecting me

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the two parts are placed together

parts.note: letters of design rearranged

indicators.note: to protect is to shield by surrounding, so one word wraps around another

parts.note: an agent acts on someone else's behalf

indicators.note: a bad version of something is a poor, jumbled one, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An agent defends a speaker while a poor design is being dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Disengagement is the act of pulling out or detaching, the noun matching withdrawing used as a noun.

clue.text: Futility that's experienced by total losers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lack of purpose or use
second meaning: the state of those who score nothing at all

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: losers whose total is zero are without points, read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Futility means having no purpose or effect, and the word also describes literally scoring nothing.

clue.text: Unwise place to stow thrones, according to a certain Reverend

definitions.text: Unwise place to stow thrones, according to a certain Reverend

parts.note: surface reading: a poor choice of storeroom for royal seats
setter's reading: swap the opening sounds to hear the proverb's action, done unwisely by those living in the place

explanation.surface: Somewhere foolish to keep a royal seat, as the Reverend might have put it.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says people who live in glass houses should not throw stones; Spooner's swap turns throw stones into stow thrones.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb warns against hypocrisy: someone living in such a fragile building should not hurl stones, making it an unwise place for that.

clue.text: Caption for illustration in story of Robin Hood, for example

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the text explaining a picture or map key

definitions.text: story of Robin Hood, for example
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a traditional tale of uncertain truth

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a picture book of Robin Hood; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the explanatory text under a picture or key on a map, and a traditional folk tale like Robin Hood's.

clue.text: Listener's set out of order in part of neighbouring country

indicators.note: things set out of order are placed in the wrong sequence, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A radio listener's set is broken somewhere in a nearby country.
explanation.walkthrough: Leinster is one of the four provinces of Ireland, the country neighbouring Britain; Dublin is in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Leinster is an eastern province of Ireland, so it is a region of Britain's next-door country.

clue.text: Ill-defined situation, with major cut covering disastrous year

indicators.note: to cover something is to go around it, so one part encloses the other
something cut is shortened, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: great means major or important

indicators.note: a disastrous outcome is a wreck, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A vague situation in which a major budget cut follows a terrible year.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is a matter that is unclear or falls between rules, an ill-defined situation.

clue.text: Brother in unspecified religious order, initially, providing cover for head

indicators.note: one item placed in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: some, as in 'some person', leaves the thing unspecified
BR is the abbreviation for brother

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word, so only those are kept

parts.note: first letters of religious and order

explanation.surface: A monk in a nameless order wears a big hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a wide-brimmed Mexican hat, a covering worn on the head.

clue.text: Book as part of normal achievement

indicators.note: the answer is one part of a longer run of letters, sitting inside these words

parts.note: letters running across the end of normal and the start of achievement

explanation.surface: A book counted as a normal accomplishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Malachi is the last book of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Malachi is the name of a book of the Bible, the final one of the minor prophets.

clue.text: Scrambled draw at home — he analysed selection, naturally

indicators.note: scrambled means jumbled together, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: letters of draw rearranged
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A messy home draw in football, with someone analysing the team selection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Selection' looks like team picking after the draw, but 'selection, naturally' is natural selection.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Darwin developed the theory of evolution by natural selection, so he is the man who studied it.

clue.text: Want to shut up snake that's venomous

indicators.note: shutting something up means enclosing it, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: to want is to wish
an asp is a small venomous snake

explanation.surface: Wanting to silence a poisonous snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venomous' seems to describe the snake, but it is the definition, in its figurative sense of spiteful.
explanation.definitionFit: Waspish means sharply irritable or spiteful, which is the figurative sense of venomous.

clue.text: Man on board provided following list of duties

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, a man on board ship
provided means on condition that, i.e. if
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A sailor on board ship is handed a list of his duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duties' looks like a sailor's tasks, but these are customs duties, taxes on goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a schedule of taxes charged on imports or exports, so a list of customs charges.

clue.text: Opportunists in sunshine outside lido rebuilt for tourists

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
one word goes outside another, wrapping around it

parts.note: from the saying 'make hay while the sun shines', meaning seize the chance
letters of lido rearranged

explanation.surface: Chancers in the sun around a rebuilt open-air pool for visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: A lido is an outdoor public swimming pool, which suits the sunny holiday scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Holidaymakers is the British word for people on vacation, so tourists is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Right conclusion produces split

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
the conclusion is the end

explanation.surface: Reaching the right conclusion causes a division.
explanation.definitionFit: To rend is to tear apart violently, a literary synonym for split.

clue.text: Revise a clue about new king or queen needing clarification

indicators.note: about means around, so the reworked letters enclose the next part
to revise is to rework, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
R stands for rex (king) or regina (queen)

explanation.surface: An editor reworking a clue about a new monarch, which needs clarifying.
explanation.walkthrough: R serves for either sex of monarch, from Latin rex and regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclear is vague or ambiguous, so it needs to be made clearer.

clue.text: List extract from minutes I meticulously sent round

indicators.note: sent round means turned to face the other way, so the letters are read backwards
an extract is a piece taken from a longer text, so the letters lie inside these words

parts.note: the run from the end of minutes, through I, to the start of meticulously

explanation.surface: A secretary sends out a carefully copied summary of the meeting minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minutes' suggests meeting notes and fits the surface, but it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to set out item by item, which is what listing something means.

clue.text: Ready to publish leaders of exceptional distinction in Telegraph

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the first letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Getting newspaper leading articles of outstanding quality ready for print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' suggests newspaper editorials, apt for the Telegraph, but here they are initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to correct and prepare it for publication.

clue.text: Artist held back by females created kind of art that's hard to believe

indicators.note: held back means turned around, so the artist's letters are read backwards
something held by others is gripped between them, so it sits inside

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female, doubled for the plural
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
etching is a printmaking art made by engraving with acid

explanation.surface: An artist restrained by women produced work no one could credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something far-fetched is improbable or exaggerated, so it strains belief.
